item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 260529
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Fri Sep 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located a few hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo
Corrientes, Mexico, on Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest
of the southern tip of Baja California, and on Hurricane Nolo,
located about 150 miles south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec (EP90):
An area of low pressure located south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec is
gradually becoming better organized. Environmental conditions are
conducive for development, and a tropical depression is expected to
form in a day or two, while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward to northwestward, parallel to the coast of
southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
A broad area of low pressure is forecast to form over the next day
or so about 1000 miles to the east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands. Environmental conditions appear favorable for gradual
development of this system, and a tropical depression could form
early next week. The system is forecast to move generally
northeastward, remaining well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Pierce/Hagen

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located
near latitude 19.1 North, longitude 123.7 West. Odalys is moving
toward the north near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this motion is expected to
continue through Saturday, followed by a turn toward the northeast
on Sunday. An eastward to southeastward motion is forecast early
next week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 115 mph (185 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Odalys is a category 3 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale. Weakening is forecast to continue through 
early next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 951 mb (28.09 inches).

None.

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 260839
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Sat Sep 26 2026

Odalys continues to show signs of weakening. Satellite imagery shows 
the hurricane's eye has been obscured by a central dense overcast 
(CDO), though microwave imagery still indicates a well-defined 
low-level circulation center. A recent 0515 UTC Metop-C 
scatterometer pass revealed an asymmetric wind field. The latest 
subjective Dvorak CI number from TAFB was 5.5/102 kt, but the 
final-T number was 5.0/90 kt. This generally aligns with most 
UW-CIMSS objective satellite intensity estimates, which range from 
98 to 106 kt. Based on a blend of these data, the initial intensity 
is lowered to 100 kt.

The initial motion is estimated to be northward, or 355/4 kt, as the 
system continues to be steered by the flow between a mid- to 
upper-level trough to its west and a mid-level ridge over northern 
Mexico. The hurricane is forecast to continue on this trajectory 
over the next day or so as the aforementioned trough amplifies over 
the eastern Pacific. By early next week, Odalys is anticipated to 
abruptly turn to the east and southeast as the increasingly shallow 
circulation becomes steered by the low-level flow. The updated track 
forecast closely aligns with the reliable HCCA consensus aid, 
nudging slightly westward prior to the sharp easterly turn, and 
remains virtually unchanged from the previous advisory thereafter.
 
The latest SHIPS guidance depicts Odalys slowly moving into a more 
unfavorable environment, characterized by moderate to strong 
vertical wind shear, mid-level dry air, and cooler sea surface 
temperatures. These conditions will likely inhibit deep convection, 
making it difficult for Odalys to remain organized later this 
weekend. Consequently, the latest NHC forecast shows Odalys 
degenerating into a post-tropical cyclone by 60 h, a trend supported 
by simulated satellite imagery from both the GFS and ECMWF.
 
Distant moisture from Hurricane Odalys and Polo will be transported
into the southwestern United States this weekend and early next
week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.

item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026 
000

TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
200 AM MST Sat Sep 26 2026
 
...POLO REMAINS AN EXTREMELY DANGEROUS CATEGORY 5 HURRICANE...
...EXPECTED TO MAKE LANDFALL IN BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR ON MONDAY AS
A POWERFUL HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM MST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.6N 111.0W
ABOUT 395 MI...640 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 375 MI...600 KM S OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...165 MPH...270 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...917 MB...27.08 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Eugenia to Santa Fe
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM MST (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located 
near latitude 17.6 North, longitude 111.0 West. Polo is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A gradual turn 
toward the northwest is expected late today and toward the north on 
Sunday. By Monday, Polo is forecast to turn northeastward and 
approach Baja California Sur.
 
Satellite images indicate that maximum sustained winds are near 165 
mph (270 km/h) with higher gusts.  Polo is an extremely dangerous 
category 5 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. 
Fluctuations in intensity are possible today. Slow weakening is 
expected to begin tonight, but Polo is expected to remain a powerful 
hurricane as it approaches Baja California Sur on Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 917 mb (27.08 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area by
Monday afternoon, with tropical storm conditions possible in the
southern portion of the watch area by Sunday night into early
Monday. These conditions are expected to spread northward during the
day on Monday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 4 to 8
inches with maximum amounts of 10 inches across portions of Baja
California Sur. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding
and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURGE: A storm surge could produce significant coastal flooding in
areas of onshore winds. Near the coast, the surge will be
accompanied by large and destructive waves.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will continue affecting the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next couple of days. Swells will also
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and the Baja
California Peninsula through the weekend. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal flooding.
Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 800 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 260256
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
800 PM MST Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Another NOAA research aircraft investigated Polo extensively this 
afternoon. The aircraft found that the minimum pressure of Polo has 
decreased slightly since the last advisory, to 911 mb. The highest 
flight-level winds measured by the aircraft were 154 kt, which 
corresponds to a 10-m wind near 140 kt. Higher instantaneous winds 
representing gusts were measured by several dropsondes, while 
another experimental instrument measured winds at near 80 m/s (155 
kt) at a height of 25 m. Since the plane flew a non-standard pattern 
on its research mission and the central pressure has actually 
slightly decreased, the intensity has been only very slightly 
lowered to 150 kt for this advisory. 
 
Fluctuations in intensity due to an eyewall replacement cycle are 
possible tonight and tomorrow, but the exact timing of such events 
can not be reliably forecast. Most guidance indicates that Polo will 
begin to gradually weaken over the next couple of days as it moves 
into a region of lower ocean heat content and encounters some 
moderate vertical wind shear. Drier environmental mid-level air 
could also contribute to weakening by the end of the weekend. 
However, it must be stressed that Polo will likely remain a 
dangerous major hurricane as it begins to approach the Baja 
California peninsula on Monday. The NHC intensity forecast remains 
on the upper end of the intensity guidance and no changes of note 
were made.

Polo has continued westward for the past several hours. There is no 
change to the track forecast reasoning with this advisory. The 
hurricane is still expected to turn gradually northwestward 
tomorrow, then northward by the end of the weekend while it moves 
around the western side of a ridge centered over northern Mexico. 
Early next week an upper-level trough approaching from the 
northwest will cause the hurricane to turn northeastward toward 
Baja California Sur and west-central Mexico. Some of NHC's most 
reliable track guidance, including the GDM and HCCA continue to be 
outliers in showing a faster track, bringing Polo to the coast of 
Baja California Sur sooner than most other guidance. Out of respect 
for this guidance, the NHC track forecast has been adjusted 
slightly faster and farther north again, but is generally very 
similar to the previous advisory.
 
Distant moisture from Hurricane Polo and Odalys will be transported
into the southwestern United States this weekend and early next
week, and may indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash
flood threat in the region. See products issued by the Weather
Prediction Center for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Polo is forecast to approach the west coast of the Baja 
California peninsula on Monday as a hurricane, and a Hurricane 
Watch is now in effect for that region. Tropical Storm conditions 
could reach portions of the coast as soon as Sunday, making further 
preparations difficult. A storm surge will be possible, especially 
in areas onshore winds.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo may begin to impact Baja
California Sur late Sunday into Monday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.

3. Dangerous surf and rip currents are likely along portions of 
the northwest coast of Mexico for the next several days.
